text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Thursday visits the Netherlands where he is expected to hold talks with his Dutch counterpart Wim Kok on Slovakia's integration with NATO and the European Union.

- Parliament on Wednesday rejected in the second reading a draft law to postpone the privatisation of the two largest commercial banks, VUB and IRB. The law was proposed by the ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), a minor partner in the ruling coalition.

- President Michal Kovac said he had received an offer whereby the Slovak police would stop investigating his and his son's alleged financial frauds if he, in return, demanded the police stop investigating the kidnapping of his son.
- Short-term money market rates rose to around 32 percent on Wednesday due to the shortage of liquidity ahead of the end of the minimum reserve requirement period on Thursday.
- Dealers said the banking sector needed some six billion crowns to meet the reserve requirement.

PRAVDA - The Constitutional Court on Wednesday rejected a government motion to postpone or cancel a referendum on direct presidential elections, saying the government had no legal authority to demand such moves.

- President Kovac welcomed the ruling of the Constitutional Court on the referendum and called for citizens to say "yes" in both upcoming plebiscites - on NATO membership and on presidential elections.
- Kovac said he expected sufficient turnout, a simple majority of all registered voters, at the two referendums scheduled for May 23 and 24.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The overall amount of classified loans in 1996 accounted for 28.8 percent of the entire balance sheet total of the Slovak banking sector, compared with 39.4 percent-share in 1995.
- Production of the Slovak engineering industry should increase to some 99 billion crowns a year by the year 2000, from around 67 billion crowns produced in 1995.
- The governemnt on Wednesday passed at a second reading a draft law on the revitalisation troubled industrial companies.
- Drotovna Hlohovec, a major Slovak steel-wire producer posted a profit of 62 million crowns in 1996. Drotovna will not pay any dividend on last year's result.

SME - Eight major opposition parties have issued a joint statement saying the policy of the ruling coalition has resulted in the exclusion of Slovakia from the first wave of NATO eastward enlargement and from the first round of integration with the EU. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
